newsitem.title: UK: NWE gas oil eases on futures as expiry halts trade.
newsitem.headline: NWE gas oil eases on futures as expiry halts trade.

text.p: NWE gas oil eased on Thursday on weaker futures but trade was minimal amid the expiry of the June IPE gas oil contract, traders said.
"There's very little going on," one trader said. "People are just waiting until the expiry's out of the way."
The June contract expired flat against Wednesday's close at $162.25 a tonne, while the July contract was trading 75 cents higher at $163.00 a tonne at 1214 GMT.
Traders expected the delivery to fairly small with estimates oscillating around the 50,000 tonne mark.
They noted, however, that exchanges for physical (EFP) deals would probably bump the unofficial delivery total up to around 200,000-250,000 tonnes.
A Wall Street trader was seen as being the main deliverer with storage material out of Antwerp.
The heating oil barge market was very quiet with second half July barges offered at July IPE +50 cents fob ARA.
Cargoes were steady with EN590 assessed at July IPE +$6.00/+$7.00 cif NWE.
Russian cargoes were still fairly weak with premiums assessed around July IPE -50 cents/+50 cents cif NWE.
